Add appropriate time-to-event outcome variables to a data frame based on the df attributes, if the file was loaded using a load function.

Source: R/add_time_to_event_variables.R
add_time_to_event_outcomes.Rd

Uses the helper functions to create three columns for an outcome defined by an event date and a censor date:

  • {prefix}_CENSOR: event date if present, otherwise censor date

  • {prefix}_BINARY: 1 if event date present, else 0

  • {prefix}_{unit}: numeric time from start_date to {prefix}_CENSOR in chosen units

Usage

add_time_to_event_outcomes(
  df,
  death_window = c("follow_up", "ascertainment"),
  ascertainment_date = NULL
)

Arguments

df

A transplant data frame from load_srtr_file(). Its file_key attribute decides which follow-up file and outcome columns are used.

death_window

Which deaths count as events, and where recipients without one are censored:

  • "follow_up" (default): deaths on or before the recipient's last follow-up date count; everyone else is censored at last follow-up.

  • "ascertainment": the SRTR program-specific report method for patient survival. Deaths from any source on or before ascertainment_date count; everyone else is assumed alive and censored at that date.

ascertainment_date

One date up to which deaths are ascertained in your SAF release, from its release notes. Required when death_window = "ascertainment".

Details

REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE keeps every death date from every source. Only the event and censoring columns (REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_BINARY, _CENSOR, _days) depend on death_window. Counting deaths found after last follow-up while censoring survivors at last follow-up would overstate mortality (#18).
